issues.description: Command names mismatch between Python and feature tests (underscore vs hyphen)
issues.detail: Python defines `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload`, which qutebrowser exposes as `:quickmarks-reload` and `:bookmarks-reload`. Existing siblings are `:quickmark-add` / `:bookmark-add` (singular). The new commands break that naming pattern — pick one shape and stick to it so users don't have to remember two conventions.

issues.description: `reload()` could be the constructor's only loader — small composition win
issues.detail: The refactor is good: `__init__` now calls `self.reload()`. But `_init_lineparser()` is still called from both `__init__` (implicitly via reload) and `reload()`. That's fine, but the reload method now owns the full load sequence — consider removing `_init_lineparser` indirection and inlining the line iteration so the data flow is one obvious function.

issues.description: No test covers removed entries on reload, only replaced ones
issues.detail: The unit test rewrites one URL to another. It doesn't verify that an entry present at construction but absent on disk at reload time is dropped, nor that a duplicate isn't double-added. Since `reload()` calls `self.marks.clear()` that's the load-bearing line — one assertion on the cleared-then-empty case would lock the contract.

Both new Gherkin scenarios start with bare `Scenario:` and no title. Every other scenario in the file is named (`Scenario: Saving a quickmark`, etc.). Costs nothing to add a name and helps test output stay greppable.

issues.description: Two near-identical command bodies — small composition opportunity
issues.detail: `quickmarks_reload` and `bookmarks_reload` are six lines each, identical except for the registry key and the message string. Not worth a class hierarchy, but a tiny helper `_reload_marks(name, label)` would make the duplication explicit and keep both commands one line. Optional — duplication this small is also fine to leave.

review.summary: Decision: SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE with one naming snag. The refactor pulls the load logic out of `__init__` into a `reload()` method on `UrlMarkManager` — that's the right shape: one function owns the data load, both construction and reload go through it, and the data structure (`OrderedDict` of marks) stays obvious. The main concern is the command names breaking the existing `:quickmark-*` / `:bookmark-*` singular convention. Minor cleanups around test coverage of the clear-on-reload contract and unnamed Gherkin scenarios. No frameworks introduced, no cleverness, no hierarchy — Pike approves the shape.
